questions.question: Tell me about yourself.
questions.questionPersian: درباره خودتان بگویید.
questions.intention: An opener to see how you summarize your professional story — not your life history.
questions.intentionPersian: می‌خواهند ببینند چطور داستان حرفه‌ای‌ات را خلاصه می‌کنی — نه زندگی‌نامه کامل.
questions.structure: Present → past → future: current role (1-2 sentences), relevant background (1-2), why you're here (1).
questions.example: I'm a backend developer with about six years of experience, currently working on payment systems at a fintech company. My background is mostly in PHP and Laravel, with hands-on experience scaling APIs. I'm here because I want to work on larger international products.
followUps: What part of your current role do you enjoy most?
What made you choose this field?

questions.question: Why are you interested in this position?
questions.questionPersian: چرا به این موقعیت علاقه دارید؟
questions.intention: They check whether you understand the role and want THIS job, not just any job.
questions.intentionPersian: می‌سنجند آیا شغل را فهمیده‌ای و همین شغل را می‌خواهی، نه هر شغلی.
questions.structure: Name 2 specific things about the role + connect them to your skills or goals. Specific beats flattering.
questions.example: Two things appeal to me: the scale of your platform, and that this role owns the API layer end to end. That aligns with what I do best, and it's the kind of technical challenge I've been looking for.
followUps: What do you know about our product?
Which part of the job description stood out to you?

questions.question: Why do you want to work for our company?
questions.questionPersian: چرا می‌خواهید در شرکت ما کار کنید؟
questions.intention: Did you research the company, and are your motivations compatible with it?
questions.intentionPersian: آیا درباره شرکت تحقیق کرده‌ای و انگیزه‌هایت با آن سازگار است؟
questions.structure: One concrete company fact (product, culture, engineering blog, market) + why it matters to you personally.
questions.example: I've followed your engineering blog for a while — the way your team handled the migration to event-driven architecture was impressive. I want to contribute to a team that works at that level and shares what it learns.
followUps: What else do you know about us?
How do you see yourself contributing in the first six months?

questions.question: What are your strengths?
questions.questionPersian: نقاط قوت شما چیست؟
questions.intention: Can you assess yourself honestly and back claims with evidence?
questions.intentionPersian: آیا می‌توانی خودت را صادقانه ارزیابی کنی و ادعایت را با شواهد پشتیبانی کنی؟
questions.structure: Pick 1-2 strengths relevant to THIS role; give one short concrete example for each.
questions.example: I'd say my main strength is debugging under pressure. For instance, last quarter I traced a payment failure that three teams had been stuck on — it turned out to be a race condition in a queue worker.
followUps: How has that strength helped your current team?
What would your colleagues say about you?

questions.question: What are your weaknesses?
questions.questionPersian: نقاط ضعف شما چیست؟
questions.intention: Self-awareness and whether you actively work on improving.
questions.intentionPersian: خودآگاهی و اینکه آیا برای بهتر شدن فعالانه تلاش می‌کنی.
questions.structure: A real (safe) weakness + what you concretely do about it. Never 'I'm a perfectionist' with no substance.
questions.example: I tend to overcommit — I say yes to too many things and then work late to deliver. I've started keeping a visible task board and discussing priorities with my manager before accepting new work, which has helped a lot.
followUps: Can you give an example of when that caused a problem?
How is the improvement going?

questions.question: Why should we hire you?
questions.questionPersian: چرا باید شما را استخدام کنیم؟
questions.intention: Your pitch: the intersection of their needs and your strengths.
questions.intentionPersian: فرصت ارائه خودت: نقطه تلاقی نیاز آن‌ها و توانایی تو.
questions.structure: Their top need → your matching proof → one differentiator. Confident, not arrogant.
questions.example: You need someone who can own the payment infrastructure from day one. I've built and operated exactly that for the past three years, so I can ramp up quickly — and I bring real production scars, not just theory.
followUps: What makes you different from other candidates?
What would you do in your first month?

questions.question: What motivates you?
questions.questionPersian: چه چیزی به شما انگیزه می‌دهد؟
questions.intention: Whether your natural motivation matches the day-to-day reality of the role.
questions.intentionPersian: آیا انگیزه طبیعی‌ات با واقعیت روزمره این شغل سازگار است؟
questions.structure: One genuine motivator + a short example of it in action. Honesty reads better than buzzwords.
questions.example: Seeing the impact of what I build. The best week of my last job was when we cut checkout failures by half and I could watch the support tickets drop day by day. Ownership of a problem from start to finish is what keeps me engaged.
followUps: What kind of work environment brings that out in you?
When were you most motivated in your career?

questions.question: Where do you see yourself in five years?
questions.questionPersian: خودتان را پنج سال دیگر کجا می‌بینید؟
questions.intention: Ambition, realism, and whether this role fits your direction (retention risk check).
questions.intentionPersian: جاه‌طلبی، واقع‌بینی و اینکه آیا این شغل در مسیر تو قرار دارد.
questions.structure: A realistic direction (deeper expertise or leadership), connected to growth THIS role offers. Avoid 'your job'.
questions.example: In five years I'd like to have grown into a senior role where I own architecture decisions and mentor other engineers. This position is a natural step — it already includes design ownership I can build on.
followUps: Are you more interested in a technical or management track?
What skills do you still want to build?

questions.question: Why are you leaving your current job?
questions.questionPersian: چرا شغل فعلی‌تان را ترک می‌کنید؟
questions.intention: Red-flag check: do you speak professionally about employers, and is your reason sound?
questions.intentionPersian: بررسی هشدارها: آیا درباره کارفرما حرفه‌ای صحبت می‌کنی و دلیلت منطقی است؟
questions.structure: Forward-looking reason (growth, scale, technology) — never complaints about people. Stay positive and brief.
questions.example: I've learned a lot there and we're on good terms, but I've outgrown the technical scope — the systems are stable and small. I'm looking for bigger scale and harder problems, which is exactly what this role offers.
followUps: What would make you stay at your current company?
What did you enjoy most there?

questions.question: What are your career goals?
questions.questionPersian: اهداف شغلی شما چیست؟
questions.intention: Direction and planning: do you drive your career or drift?
questions.intentionPersian: جهت‌گیری و برنامه‌ریزی: آیا مسیر شغلی‌ات را خودت هدایت می‌کنی؟
questions.structure: One short-term goal (next 1-2 years) + one long-term direction, both plausible from this role.
questions.example: Short term, I want to get genuinely strong at distributed systems — that's the next gap in my skills. Long term I'm working towards a staff-level role where I set technical direction across teams.
followUps: How does this position fit those goals?
What are you doing right now to work towards them?

questions.question: How do you handle stress and pressure?
questions.questionPersian: با استرس و فشار چطور کنار می‌آیید؟
questions.intention: Whether you have real coping strategies or fall apart (or pretend stress doesn't exist).
questions.intentionPersian: آیا راهبرد واقعی برای مدیریت فشار داری یا وانمود می‌کنی استرس وجود ندارد.
questions.structure: Your concrete method (prioritize, break down, communicate) + one quick example.
questions.example: I break the problem down and prioritize ruthlessly. During our worst outage, I listed what we knew, assigned one thread per person, and kept the status channel updated every fifteen minutes. Structure keeps me calm.
followUps: Tell me about the most stressful situation you've handled.
How do you prevent burnout?

questions.question: Do you prefer working alone or in a team?
questions.questionPersian: کار فردی را ترجیح می‌دهید یا تیمی؟
questions.intention: Team-fit check. The honest answer is almost always 'both, depending on the task'.
questions.intentionPersian: بررسی تناسب تیمی. جواب صادقانه تقریباً همیشه «هر دو، بسته به کار» است.

vocabulary.persian: ایده‌ها را با کسی محک زدن

questions.structure: Both, with examples: when you seek the team, when you need focus. Show flexibility.
questions.example: Honestly, both — it depends on the task. For design decisions I want the team: I like bouncing ideas off people. For implementation I need blocks of deep focus. A good week has both.
followUps: How do you handle disagreements in a team?
Describe your ideal team.

questions.question: How do you respond to criticism?
questions.questionPersian: به انتقاد چطور واکنش نشان می‌دهید؟
questions.intention: Coachability — can they give you feedback without drama?
questions.intentionPersian: قابلیت یادگیری — آیا می‌شود بدون حاشیه به تو بازخورد داد؟
questions.structure: Your attitude (welcome it, don't take it personally) + one example where feedback changed your behavior.
questions.example: I genuinely want it — vague praise teaches me nothing. In my last review my manager said my PR descriptions were too thin for reviewers. I built a small template, and review turnaround on my PRs dropped noticeably. I'd rather hear it early than late.
followUps: Tell me about feedback that was hard to hear.
How do you give criticism to others?

questions.question: What do you know about our company?
questions.questionPersian: درباره شرکت ما چه می‌دانید؟
questions.intention: Pure homework check. No research reads as no genuine interest.
questions.intentionPersian: بررسی تحقیق قبلی. تحقیق‌نکردن یعنی علاقه واقعی نداری.
questions.structure: 2-3 specific facts (product, market, recent news) + one honest question you still have.
questions.example: You build logistics software for mid-size retailers — as far as I know, around two hundred customers across Europe — and you recently launched the route-optimization product. I'm curious how big the engineering team behind that launch was, actually.
followUps: What interests you about our market?
Have you used our product?

questions.question: What is your greatest professional achievement?
questions.questionPersian: بزرگ‌ترین دستاورد حرفه‌ای شما چیست؟
questions.intention: What you consider success, and whether you can tell a results-focused story.
questions.intentionPersian: تعریف تو از موفقیت و توانایی روایت نتیجه‌محور.
questions.structure: Mini-STAR: context in one sentence, what YOU did, measurable result. Your real achievement, modest numbers are fine.
questions.example: Rebuilding our deployment pipeline. Releases used to take a full day and fail often; I introduced staged rollouts and automated checks. Deploys went from weekly and scary to daily and boring — that 'boring' is what I'm proudest of.
followUps: What was the hardest part of that work?
Who else was involved?

questions.question: How would your colleagues describe you?
questions.questionPersian: همکارانتان شما را چطور توصیف می‌کنند؟
questions.intention: Self-awareness from an outside angle; consistency with the rest of your answers.
questions.intentionPersian: خودآگاهی از نگاه دیگران و هم‌خوانی با بقیه پاسخ‌هایت.
questions.structure: 2-3 adjectives with tiny proof ('I'm usually the go-to person for X'). Attribute them to colleagues, keep it humble.
questions.example: They'd probably say reliable and straightforward — if I commit to a date, it ships. I've also become the go-to person for anything queue-related, which I take as a compliment about being approachable.
followUps: What would they say you could improve?
What role do you naturally take in a team?

questions.question: What kind of work environment do you prefer?
questions.questionPersian: چه محیط کاری را ترجیح می‌دهید؟
questions.intention: Culture-fit: will you actually be happy and productive here?
questions.intentionPersian: تناسب فرهنگی: آیا واقعاً اینجا راضی و موثر خواهی بود؟
questions.structure: 2-3 genuine conditions you work best in; ideally ones this company plausibly offers. Honesty protects you too.
questions.example: I thrive with autonomy plus clear expectations — tell me the outcome and the deadline, and trust me on the how. I also value open communication: problems discussed early, not hidden until the deadline.
followUps: How do you handle an environment that isn't like that?
What's one thing your current team does well?

questions.question: Do you have any questions for us?
questions.questionPersian: سوالی از ما دارید؟
questions.intention: 'No' signals low interest. Good questions show how you think.
questions.intentionPersian: «نه» یعنی علاقه کم. سوال خوب نشان می‌دهد چطور فکر می‌کنی.
questions.structure: Always ask 2-3. Best topics: day-to-day reality, success criteria, team challenges — not salary (yet).
questions.example: Yes — I'd love to know what the first three months look like day-to-day, and how you measure success for this role at the one-year mark. Also, what's the team's biggest technical challenge right now?

questions.question: When can you start?
questions.questionPersian: از کی می‌توانید شروع کنید؟
questions.intention: Practical logistics — and whether you treat your current employer professionally.
questions.intentionPersian: موضوع عملی — و اینکه با کارفرمای فعلی حرفه‌ای رفتار می‌کنی یا نه.
questions.structure: State your notice period plainly; a clean handover is a POSITIVE signal, don't apologize for it.
questions.example: I have a one-month notice period, and I'd want to hand over my projects properly — so I'd be available from the first of next month. If needed, I could start part-time earlier.
followUps: Is the notice period negotiable?
Would you be open to starting earlier?

questions.question: Tell me about a time you failed.
questions.questionPersian: از زمانی بگویید که شکست خوردید.
questions.intention: Honesty, accountability, and whether failure actually changed your behavior.
questions.intentionPersian: صداقت، مسئولیت‌پذیری و اینکه آیا شکست رفتارت را واقعاً تغییر داد.
questions.structure: A real failure (yours, not the team's), what it cost, what you changed. Blame nobody else.
questions.example: I once shipped a schema migration without a rollback plan — I'd underestimated the data volume, and we had twenty minutes of downtime. Entirely my call. Since then every migration I write ships with a tested rollback, no exceptions.
followUps: How did your team react?
What would you do differently today?
